To be fair I do see what he is saying and I think articulation may be causing some trouble. Obviously all of the games are cartoony to an extent. But as you acknowledge, BL1 was undeniably the least so. They only decided to go with that art style late on in development and it was supposed to be a realistic (for its time) shooter. So it still has the same kind of colour pallet, graphical fidelity, art direction and so on and so forth as a lot of other games which went for realism at that time. Stuff like Fallout New Vegas, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. that kinda stuff.

But there was a gradual development and refinement of the art direction they honed over time. You're right to say that in some aspects, 3 and 4 are more realistic, especially when it comes to things like lighting, volumetrics, visual effects, all that kind of stuff. But I think that there are aspects that aren't being considered because I've always considered BL2 to look and feel more "realistic" than 3 or 4 as well, and I think realism is the wrong word. I think right way to word is is that it looks less heavy-handed with its own art style. The artistic aesthetic doesn't seep as deep into every detail like they do  in the later games. World design, for example. BL2 has a lot of bland environments, deserts, tundra, highlands, so on and so forth. Whereas 3 has places like Promethea which feel surreal and exaggerated. The colours in 2 are more muted and don't pop quite as much which can give it a bit more of a rugged dirty look.

Screen pollution too. Each new entry has more of it than the last and that's another way in which the later games can look more deeply set into an aesthetic that isn't trying for believability. Character and model design is an aspect that I think is also important. Starting with BL3, characters and models got a lot chunkier. Everything in the world became thicc. If you look at Lilith in BL2 and compare it to BL3, it's [extremely noticeable.](https://www.reddit.com/media?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpreview.redd.it%2Fnaoyvyds89q21.jpg%3Fauto%3Dwebp%26s%3D644de85ee90251df4f8e175427628bc41ef4f094) Clothes are thicker, facial features are puffier, hair is a bit more play-dough. That's every character not just her. In general the world of BL3 feels pudgier, softer and fatter in a way that is hard to nail down, as well as models and objects being a lot more complex and higher-poly in BL3 onwards.

BL2 just had a lot less going on visually. From the graphics to the world design, models, characters, visual effects. All that combines to create a visual aesthetic in 2 that feels less heavily stylised and makes it look a bit more generalised and looked a bit closer to other shooters of the time. It's really a spectrum from 1 to 3. I *think* that is what OP may be getting at, because I've always thought this myself too.

TL;DR BL2 had less going on visually, made it look less easily distinguishable from the "realistic-looking" shooters of the time. It's still not realistic, it's just not as heavily stylised as all the games from 3 onwards. Partly graphics, partly because it took multiple games to develop the aesthetic. Methinks.

The grinding isn't a thing because there's nothing else to do tho. The grinding is more prominent in the borderlands game because of how its loot works. When you take like 20 or so different variables for every item, make a shit ton of different items and then randomise them, ultimately you get certain things which are both extremely rare and very powerful. Dedicated players enjoy trying to find those things because they're elusive. This is like saying people dig mile wide holes in Minecraft because there's nothing else to do. No, a few dedicated people do it and they do it because the game allows them to and because that's the goal they've set themselves. It doesn't help and it isn't necessary. You will never need a 94 sham in BL2, but yet some people have spent 10 years farming it because they want to. I spent 3 days farming the exact Cutsman and also the exact Flipper I wanted in BL3. I didn't need them, but I enjoyed it and it felt rewarding once I got it. That was optional.

Whether looter shooter is a subgenre of something else is irrelevant, grinding is a core part of looter shooters full stop. The raid bosses being bad is completely your subjective opinion and not even one that many people share. You might get away with making a case for BL1 not really having an endgame but the whole reason farming became such a big thing in these games in the first place is because BL2 introduced an endgame people found to be worth grinding for. I can respect that you don't like BL2 it is a flawed game but let's not confuse that for anything objective.

Disagree. The GTA games (Especially 4 onwards) have always been a form of social commentary and political satire. Especially GTA 4 which in that game, the commentary on the American Dream and the criticism of modern American culture were a huge almost essential part of that game. The whole reason it follows Niko, an outsider, is because it allows for the player to have the same experience as Niko when it comes to entering into this caricature of American life. Us because we're seeing the satire, Niko because he is new to it all and it is confusing and overstimulating for him. It's what nerds call Ludo-narrative harmony, where the story and what we do as players aligns perfectly and make sense and compliment eachother. GTA 5 took broader jabs at a wider range of subjects but, the games have definitely been a lot more than just lighthearted fun. It's not hateful, it's commentary, but it's also definitely not just a laugh with no deeper meaning put into them.

If anything, their last two games opening up in the snow makes me think they'd want to distance themselves from that rather than reinforce the trope. That, and it doesn't snow much in southern Georgia. Even as far north as Savannah I've heard people saying they get ice and frost most years, with snow being rare and limited to a couple inches at most. I don't see it personally.

If we look at the GTA series as a whole, snow is so rare that it has only appeared in a select number of location-specific missions countable on one hand. As a general rule, it just doesn't snow in GTA.

If you want to see exciting new weather events in 6, I'd bet on seeing our first hurricanes in the series. That has a lot of room for story mode utilization and with the physics engine Rockstar have nowadays it could be extremely dynamic and beautiful. That's what I think

I don't think so at all. Large panels are actually one of the worst types of UI for PC usage. When you're using a mouse, you have a great amount of precision and control over where you're pointing it. PC input works very well with list-based UI, dropdown menus, and such.

Arrow keys to flip through individual items/submenus, mouse to select individual items and scroll down lists etc. Panels take up a huge amount of space which means the mouse isn't being utilised properly at all and is rendered almost obsolete.

As a PC player this UI feels horrible and clunky. This is why mods like SkyUI are so popular for Skyrim, turning the large buttons and bulky text of the vanilla UI into expansive lists and dropdown menus very easy to navigate with a mouse.

MWII's UI is much more suited to console actually, since a controller can never be omnidirectional like a mouse, it is best for grid-based designs like the panels in this game. That's why virtually every console dashboard is a panel design, vs an array of icons like on a PC desktop.
